ancestries.name: Human
ancestries.blurb: Humans are restless, adaptable, and ambitious, making much of their brief lives and finding strength in one another.
bloodlines: You gain the Rally Aura: The first time each round an ally within 15 feet who can see you defends against an Attack with the Fear trait, they gain a +1 Situation bonus to that Defense check.

lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Humans are restless, adaptable, and ambitious, making much of their brief lives and finding strength in one another.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Humans are everywhere, and everywhere they are different. No other people spreads so far, argues so loudly, or reinvents itself so often. A human border town can change its laws, its faith, and its skyline inside a single generation; an elf who naps through a decade returns to find the maps redrawn. What humans lack in long memory they repay in momentum, and the other peoples watch them with a mix of admiration and alarm.

That restlessness is personal as much as cultural. A human feels the shortness of their years and answers it with ambition: one more field cleared, one more deal struck, one more mountain nobody sensible would climb. At their best, humans bind strangers into companies and companies into causes. At their worst, they burn through places, promises, and people the way they burn through years.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who can come from anywhere, get along with anyone, and refuse to stay in any lane, you should play a human.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
• Chase a goal so hard that rest starts to feel like theft.
• Collect skills, contacts, and causes the way others collect coins.
• Assume any problem can be solved if you just find the right people for it.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
• Envy how quickly you learn, adapt, and move on.
• Wonder what you are running from, or racing toward.
• Trust your knack for finding common ground, even between old enemies.

lore.label: Physical Description (at a glance)
lore.text: Humans are middling in most measures and wildly varied in all of them. They stand roughly five to six and a half feet tall, in every build from wiry to broad, with skin, hair, and eyes spanning every shade their homelands offer. What marks a human crowd is not a shared look but a shared motion: quick eyes, busy hands, and clothing that borrows freely from every neighbor they have ever traded with.

lore.label: Physical Description (life cycle)
lore.text: Humans reach physical adulthood around 15 years and are usually granted a place at the adults' table by 18, though every town draws that line differently. A human who avoids war, plague, and their own ambition can expect sixty to ninety years, and a rare few see a century. Their short season is the quiet engine of their character; humans plant orchards whose shade they will never sit in, and they know it.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
Human society is less a single design than a permanent argument about what the design should be. Kingdoms, leagues, free towns, wandering companies: humans have tried them all, usually at the same time, usually within a week's ride of each other. Their gift is the joining of strangers. A human market will seat a dwarven smith beside an elven dyer and a gnomish clockmaker, and by closing time the three will share a ledger and a grudge against the harbormaster.

Because they invent themselves so freely, humans put enormous weight on names, oaths, and reputations, the few things that outlive them. A human's word, once given before witnesses, is a load-bearing wall; whole towns stand on webs of such promises. Breaking one is not just a sin but a kind of vandalism.

Humans honor their dead by continuing their projects. Workshops, farms, feuds, and half-built bridges pass from hand to hand like torches, and a human family can often recite what each generation added to the house even when they have forgotten the builders' faces.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text: Human belief runs hot and plural. One village keeps six shrines and hedges its bets at all of them; the next follows a single creed with terrifying focus. What is consistent is the human conviction that effort matters, that the world is unfinished, and that somebody, probably them, ought to get on with finishing it. Their prayers tend to be practical: strength for the harvest, luck for the crossing, courage for the morning.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
• Leave every place better than you found it.
• Keep your word once witnesses have heard it.
• Lift the newcomer; you were one once.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
• Waste a year owed to the people who raised you.
• Break a promise made before witnesses.
• Let fear of failing keep you from beginning.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Human given names vary widely between families and homelands. Many human surnames preserve an ancestor’s occupation, carrying the memory of a workshop, livelihood, or useful skill through generations. A family named Cooper might have stopped making barrels centuries ago, yet still treasure the name.

Common given names Alden, Bram, Cassia, Doran, Elsbeth, Garron, Hale, Imre, Joss, Lysa, Mara, Oren, Sera, Tavin, Wren, Ysolde.

Common surnames Baker, Carter, Cooper, Fletcher, Mason, Miller, Roper, Tanner, Turner, Weaver.

Example names Alden Cooper, Cassia Fletcher, Elsbeth Weaver, Garron Mason, Lysa Carter, Tavin Roper.

cultures.name: Serrovane
cultures.blurb: Serrovanians build trust through witnessed promises, careful records, and the conviction that a person should answer for their word.

lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Serrovanians build trust through witnessed promises, careful records, and the conviction that a person should answer for their word.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Serrovane is a lowland order-state of cultivated fields, raised roads, and towns gathered around registry halls. Its ledgers are kept in triplicate, its agreements carry witnesses, and its disputes follow forms that everyone is expected to respect. A promise spoken casually may be forgotten. A promise entered into the record becomes something other people can build their lives upon.

People of many ancestries belong to this order. An elven witness, a dwarven magistrate, and a human challenger may disagree bitterly while trusting the same record. Serrovanians learn how to state a grievance, acknowledge an obligation, and offer a concession without surrendering their standing. They can be formidable negotiators: they know exactly what they have promised, and they expect you to know the same.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who takes promises seriously, understands the power of public reputation, and can turn a few carefully chosen words into a lasting obligation, choose Serrovane.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
• Ask who witnessed an agreement before asking whether it was a good one.
• Carry copies of important promises, judgments, or introductions among your belongings.
• Insist on settling the terms of a contest before anyone draws a weapon.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
• Trust you to remember an obligation long after everyone else has forgotten it.
• Find your careful questions reassuring, exhausting, or faintly threatening.
• Worry that an innocent remark might become a commitment in your hearing.

lore.label: Dress and Bearing
lore.text:
Serrovanian clothing favors orderly layers, durable fabrics, and visible signs of affiliation. Household colors, office badges, and witness cords help others recognize whom a person represents. Garments vary with ancestry, occupation, and means, but people generally take care that closures are secure and identifying marks remain legible.

Formal bearing matters as much as fine clothing. Standing to acknowledge a witness, leaving another speaker room to finish, and presenting a document with clean hands all communicate respect.

lore.label: Upbringing and Milestones
lore.text:
Children learn promises through ordinary responsibilities: returning borrowed tools, delivering messages accurately, and admitting when a task remains unfinished. Many households preserve a young person’s first independently witnessed obligation.

Public responsibility follows demonstrated judgment, with its timing shaped by ancestry and family custom. Taking an office, joining a household, completing an apprenticeship, and retiring from service are commonly marked by a formal acknowledgment of the duties being accepted or released.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
Serrovanian institutions depend on recorded responsibilities. Officials swear to the limits of their offices, guilds preserve the terms of their charters, and households keep accounts of debts, inheritances, and obligations. Public scribes and witnesses are familiar figures in markets and village squares.

Formal challenge gives disputes an accepted shape. The grievance, the contest, and the consequences are declared before witnesses. Some challenges involve arms; others test skill, testimony, or the ability to substantiate a claim. Violence within accepted terms can be lawful. Breaking those terms threatens the trust that made the challenge possible.

This order has its cruelties. Wealth buys patient advocates, old records can preserve old injustices, and a precisely worded agreement can conceal an ugly intention. Serrovanians argue fiercely over whether justice lies in honoring the record or correcting what should never have been written into it.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text:
Serrovanians follow many faiths, but promises, testimony, and remembrance occupy an honored place across them. Shrines often witness marriages, reconciliations, and vows of service. An ancestor may be remembered through an obligation their descendants continue to uphold.

Mercy also has a recognized dignity. Publicly releasing someone from an oath can be an act of generosity remembered as long as the oath itself.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
• Keep your word when doing so becomes inconvenient.
• State your terms before the contest begins.
• Stand witness when another needs the truth recorded.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
• Knowingly swear an oath you intend to break.
• Falsify a record entrusted to your care.
• Inflict punishment beyond the terms of an accepted challenge.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Many Serrovanian surnames take the form of a short promise: something a household declares it will uphold. These names are inherited, and families take particular pride in living up to them. Someone named Speaktrue can expect a lie to be remembered with unusual clarity.

People commonly retain given names from their family or ancestry. The surnames below are familiar Common translations of Serrovine names.

Common given names Cerran, Dovra, Ilyra, Maroven, Orven, Selka, Tavren, Veyra.

Common surnames Bearwitness, Holdfaith, Keepword, Speaktrue, Standfast.

Example names Cerran Keepword, Dovra Standfast, Ilyra Speaktrue, Maroven Bearwitness, Selka Holdfaith.

cultures.name: Kestrel Reach
cultures.blurb: Reachers thrive where people and possibilities meet, building livelihoods through sharp observation, useful introductions, and bargains worth making again.

lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Reachers thrive where people and possibilities meet, building livelihoods through sharp observation, useful introductions, and bargains worth making again.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Kestrel Reach spreads across a wide river delta, where channels divide around crowded islands and trade-towns rise above the floodwater. Six languages may be spoken along a single dock, with three more heard by evening. Boats bring unfamiliar goods, travelers bring unfamiliar customs, and someone is always looking for a person who understands both.

Reachers grow accustomed to difference early. An elven shipwright, a dwarven grain factor, and a human ferryman may share a neighborhood, a business venture, and a running argument about harbor fees. Local knowledge means knowing how people prefer to be approached, which courtesies matter to them, and whom they trust to make an introduction. A good broker can accomplish with an afternoon’s conversation what an armed company might spend a season making worse.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who is comfortable among unfamiliar faces, always listening for an opportunity, and rarely without someone they could ask for help, choose Kestrel Reach.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
Learn a few useful words whenever you encounter a new language.
Introduce yourself by naming someone the other person already knows.
Look for what each side needs before deciding that a dispute cannot be settled.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
Expect you to know a useful contact in almost any port.
Wonder whether your friendly questions are leading toward a proposal.
Rely on you to notice the custom, omission, or hidden cost they overlooked.

lore.label: Dress and Bearing
lore.text:
Reach clothing reflects crowded docks, changeable weather, and goods arriving from distant places. Practical layers, secure pockets, broad hats, and garments kept clear of ropes are common. Fabrics and ornaments travel freely between communities, adapted to each wearer’s build and family traditions.

Reachers often display a token of their trade, vessel, or trading house where an acquaintance can recognize it. Greeting gestures vary between neighborhoods, and knowing which one to offer can make a warmer introduction than expensive clothes.

lore.label: Upbringing and Milestones
lore.text:
Young Reachers learn by carrying messages, helping with household business, and accompanying experienced relatives through markets and landing places. They are taught to notice who has spoken, who has been overlooked, and whether everyone understands the same terms.

A first independently completed bargain or entrusted journey often marks growing responsibility. Its importance lies in returning with the agreement fulfilled and the other party willing to deal with the household again. These milestones follow readiness and circumstance across the Reach’s many ancestries.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
The delta depends on cooperation that extends beyond individual towns. Ferrymen need maintained channels, merchants need dependable warehouses, and everyone needs the flood banks to hold. Neighborhood associations, trading houses, craft guilds, and harbor officials overlap in a web of favors and competing responsibilities.

Reputation moves quickly along the waterways. A generous settlement can bring business from three towns away; a cheated customer can arrive ahead of you wherever you hoped to trade next. Brokers earn their standing by remembering details, protecting confidences, and finding terms that people will actually honor.

The Reach’s friendliness can conceal hard boundaries. Established houses sometimes keep profitable routes among themselves, and an introduction may matter more than an excellent offer. Reachers admire people who open opportunities for others, but they also know how easily a well-connected few can decide who gets a place at the table.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text:
Reach shrines welcome travelers, returning crews, and families whose traditions came from elsewhere. River spirits, ancestral patrons, and gods of craft, fortune, and safe passage all receive offerings.

Many Reachers regard hospitality as an obligation that travels. Someone shelters a stranger today because another household may shelter their own kin tomorrow. Gifts, favors, and acts of kindness create relationships whose value cannot always be entered into an account.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
Learn how to greet people on their own terms.
Give the other party a reason to trade with you again.
Share a useful introduction when it costs you little.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
Abuse the protection offered to a guest.
Conceal a danger that makes an agreement impossible to fulfill.
Betray a confidence entrusted to you as a broker.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Reach surnames often come from waterways and shoreline features. A name may remember the bank where a household built its first home, the channel its boats worked, or the landing from which its members scattered across the world. Families carry these names inland long after the river itself has become a distant memory.

Given names mingle freely across languages and ancestries. The surnames below are commonly used in their Common forms.

Common given names Avi, Dena, Jori, Kes, Lio, Mira, Neris, Orren, Savi, Tavi.

Common surnames Broadwater, Lowbank, Northbank, Reedbank, Siltwater, Stillwater, Three-Tides, Willowbend.

Example names Avi Northbank, Dena Willowbend, Jori Reedbank, Mira Three-Tides, Neris Stillwater, Tavi Lowbank.

backgrounds: In a circus or on the streets, you earned your pay by performing as an acrobat. You might have turned to adventuring when the money dried up, or simply decided to put your skills to better use.

You served in somebody's army: a levy, a free company, a city watch that saw real fighting. You learned the drill, the marching, and the waiting, and you learned what a line looks like just before it breaks.

You made your living outside the law, whether by picking pockets, running contraband, or talking your way through doors that were meant to stay shut. You still know who to ask, and which questions never to.

While properly Fitted, the piece functions as Flexible.
Attended
Donning and doffing without help takes twice as long.
Brimmed
Gain +1 Protection against ranged attacks to this Zone.
Comfort
May be slept in without armor-induced Fatigue.
Concealable
Can be hidden beneath ordinary clothing or headwear unless closely inspected.
Fitted
If you wear armor with the Fitted trait in at least three Zones, and they have all been adjusted to you, reduce total Load Strain by 1.
Flexible

Treat this piece’s Load as 1 lower for checks relying on that zone’s full range of motion, such as Climb or Swim. It still counts fully for other Load Strain-related penalties, such as Rush, Leap, Acrobatics, and Stealth.
Muffled
Its fabric-covered construction never contributes to Clatter, even if damaged or worn loosely.
Noisy
Imposes a -1 cumulative Gear penalty to Stealth for each piece of Noisy gear equipped.
Open
Does not impair Awareness, breathing, speech, or visible spell targeting.
Repairable
A damaged piece may be restored during a rest with appropriate plates, cord, rivets, or tools; no full armorer’s workshop is required.
Visored
Can Raise or Lower the visor as a single action. Lowered: Imposes –1 Gear penalty to Awareness and Initiative. Raised: Protection is reduced by 1, but no Awareness or Initiative penalties.
actionTraits: Attack
An action a foe answers with a Defense. Attacks are resolved as Exchanges (see Chapter 4: The Exchange). A Committed Strike ❸ is also Weighted.
Auditory
It works through sound. It fails on the deafened, and on anyone who cannot hear you.
Concentrate
Maneuvers with this Trait take an extra action to complete if you are Heedless.
Emotion
A mental effect that works on feeling. Anything immune to emotion ignores it.
Flexible
A weapon that cannot Parry, form a Bind, or be Bound.
Manipulate
You use your hands. You need at least one free, and fine work near an enemy can provoke a Reaction from them.
Massive
An attack so heavy that any Critical Hit Wounds, whether or not the Zone was Exposed. Reserved for the largest creatures.
Mental
It works on the mind. It fails on anything mindless.
Motion

You change position under your own power. Moving into a foe’s Total Reach may provoke an Intercept from that foe; moving out of it may provoke a Reaction from anyone with a Talent that allows it. Step does neither.
Press

Actions with this trait follow up an earlier attack. You can use a Press action only if your previous action this round was a Strike against the same target, and only at your own Opportunity. Some actions with the Press trait also grant an effect on a failure. The effects that are added on a failure don’t apply on a critical failure. If your Press action succeeds, you can choose to apply the failure effect instead (for example, when an attack deals no damage due to resistance).
Prepared
A Maneuver of three or more actions. Spend one action now and reserve the rest; it resolves at your next Opportunity (see Encounter Mode).
Posture
A special type of Reaction that doesn’t cost any actions. Any Zones Exposed by a Posture remain Exposed until the end of the round.
Reaction

A Maneuver you may perform outside your Opportunity, the moment its Trigger occurs. It costs its listed actions from the same six as everything else, and you may use as many Reactions in a round as you can afford. A Reaction never triggers another Reaction. Marked ↺ beside its cost.
Stance
A way of standing and holding yourself. You can be in only one stance at a time, and it lasts until you leave it, fall unconscious, or enter another.
Unparryable
An attack that cannot be answered with Parry and offers nothing to Bind. Guard still applies to it.
Weighted
A Committed Strike ❸. If it is Stopped (a Graze or a Miss), you are Exposed in a Zone of the defender’s choice.
Visual
It works through sight. It fails on the blinded, and on anyone who cannot see you.

❶ Quick. A probe: one weapon die plus precision damage, nothing else, on the Torso. It cannot Critically Hit (Agile weapons excepted) and Protection applies in full even to an Exposed Zone. Stopped, it costs you nothing and can only be bound, never Controlled.
❷ Deliberate. All dice, specialization, and your Might. It may be placed on an Exposed Zone, and on a Critical Hit you may Expose a plausible Zone. A Graze costs only the tempo; on a Miss you are Exposed. A Parry that Stops it takes Control.
❸ Committed. Prepared. All dice, specialization, and your Might. On a Hit or Critical Hit, you may Expose a plausible Zone. Weighted: Stopped, Graze or Miss, you are Exposed. A Parry that Stops it takes Control.

Requirements A rigid weapon, shield, or permitted natural weapon in hand; the target's weapon or natural attack is within the longer of your two Total Reaches; the target is no more than one Size larger than you.
Roll Melee against the target's Guard.
Critical Success You Control the weapon, and the target is Off-Guard until its next Opportunity. Success You Control the weapon. Graze A neutral Bind forms. Miss You pressed badly. The target Controls your weapon instead.
Special Evade cannot answer this attack. While you Control a weapon, the target has an Exposed Zone of your choice and takes −2 Situation to attacks with it (see Chapter 2: The Exchange).

Requirements You Control a foe's weapon.
Step toward that foe. The Bind holds, and the Controlled weapon cannot Intercept you. This is the only movement that does not end a Bind.

Requirements You have a free hand or a weapon with the Grapple Trait, and the target must be within reach and no more than one Size larger than you.
Roll Athletics against Evade or Guard.
Critical Success The target is Restrained until the end of the next round. Success The target is Grabbed until the end of the next round. Graze No effect. Miss You overcommit and are Off-Guard until your next Opportunity.
❷ Tackle. Move, then Grapple. Critical Success The target is Restrained until the end of the next round and knocked Prone. Success The target is Grabbed until the end of the next round and knocked Prone. You fall Prone adjacent to them. Graze No effect, and you are Exposed in a Zone of the defender's choice. Miss You overcommit and are Off-Guard until your next Opportunity, and fall Prone adjacent to them.

Requirements You have a free hand or a weapon with the Shove Trait, and the target must be within reach and no more than one Size larger than you.
Roll Athletics against Evade or Guard.
Critical Success The target is pushed 6 feet. You may Move as part of this action, if it is in the same direction. Success The target is pushed 3 feet. Graze No effect. Miss You overcommit and are Off-Guard until your next Opportunity.
❷ Heave. You set your feet and put your weight behind it. Critical Success The target is pushed 12 feet. Success The target is pushed 6 feet. Graze No effect, and you are Exposed in a Zone of the defender's choice. Miss You overcommit and are Off-Guard until your next Opportunity.

Requirements You have a free hand or a weapon with the Trip Trait, and the target must be within reach and no more than one Size larger than you.
Roll Athletics against Evade or Guard.
Critical Success The target is knocked Prone, and takes damage equal to your Might. Success The target is knocked Prone. Graze No effect. Miss You overcommit and are Off-Guard until your next Opportunity.
Special If the target's Legs are Exposed, increase the degree of success by one.
❷ Leg Sweep. Critical Success The target is knocked Prone, takes damage equal to your Might, and becomes Exposed [Legs]. Success The target is knocked Prone and becomes Exposed [Legs]. Graze No effect, and you are Exposed in a Zone of the defender's choice. Miss You overcommit and are Off-Guard until your next Opportunity. The Special above still applies.

Requirements You have a free hand or a weapon with the Disarm Trait, and the target must be within reach and no more than one Size larger than you.
Roll Athletics against Evade or Guard.
Critical Success The item drops from their grip and lands in one of their squares. Success Their grip is loosened: −2 Situation penalty to attacks with it, and the next Disarm against them gains a +2 Situation bonus, until they spend an Interact to resettle it. Graze No effect. Miss You overcommit and are Off-Guard until your next Opportunity.
Special If the target's Arms are Exposed, increase the degree of success by one.
❸ Wrench. Critical Success The item flies from their grip and lands 1d10 squares away, in a direction of your choosing. Success The item drops from their grip and lands in one of their squares. Graze No effect, and you are Exposed in a Zone of the defender's choice. Miss You overcommit and are Off-Guard until your next Opportunity. The Special above still applies.

Requirements You have a free hand or are already Grabbing or Restraining the target, and the target must be within reach and no more than one Size larger than you.
Roll Athletics against Evade or Guard.
Critical Success Move the target up to 6 feet, staying within your reach, not into or through obstacles. Success Move the target up to 3 feet, staying within your reach, not into or through obstacles. Graze No effect. Miss The target can move you up to 3 feet as though it Repositioned you.
❷ Haul. Critical Success Move up to your full Speed, bringing the target with you. Success Move up to half your Speed, bringing the target with you. Graze No effect, and you are Exposed in a Zone of the defender's choice. Miss The target can move you up to 6 feet the same way.
Defense & Recovery: Gain your shield's Gear bonus to Guard until your next Opportunity. You must be wielding it.
Gather yourself: clear every Exposed Zone on you (except one Exposed by a Posture) and end any Bind you are in.

Requirements You have Cover, or Greater Cover, or are wielding a tower shield.
Press yourself into your cover. Your Cover improves by one grade. Adjust the Zones Covered to match. This lasts until you Move, Step or Attack.
Special A raised tower shield gives you Cover with nothing to get behind, so Taking Cover behind one gives you Greater Cover.

Break free of a grab, a restraint, or anything holding you.
Requirements You are Grabbed or Restrained.
Roll your best of Athletics or Acrobatics against the grabber's Endure.
Critical Success You are no longer Grabbed or Restrained, and may Step ⓿. Success You are no longer Grabbed or Restrained. Failure The Grabbed or Restrained condition persists. Critical Failure The condition persists and their hold improves: if you were Grabbed, you are now Restrained.

Move up to half your Speed. Step has no Traits at all, which is the point: it never provokes Intercepts or other Reactions. Stepping ends any Bind you are in (Close excepted). You cannot Step into difficult terrain.

Requirements You have Guard Training, and a rigid weapon, shield, or permitted natural weapon in hand.
Answer an attack with Guard at a +2 Situation bonus. If you Stop a Deliberate or Committed Strike, you take Control of the attacking weapon instead of forming a neutral Bind, and you may at once make a Quick Strike ⓿ against its owner (the riposte). A Stopped Quick Strike gives only a neutral Bind.

Requirements You have Evade Training.
Answer an attack with Evade at a +2 Situation bonus. If the attack is Stopped, you may Step in any direction.

Requirements You are Expert in Melee; the attacker is within your Reach and the attack is a melee attack.
Answer the attack with a Quick Strike of your own. You gain no bonus to your Defense. Roll both; resolve both. You cannot Counter a Counter or an Intercept, and the fighter you Counter rolls only their basic Defense against it.

Requirements You have Melee Training.
Trigger A foe Moves from outside your Total Reach to inside it, or Strikes you with an Unwieldy weapon from inside its Unwieldy distance.
Make a Quick Strike against them at the moment they enter. Once per foe per Move. A Wound stops their movement; anything less and it continues.
Do nothing at this Opportunity. You may still use Reactions. When a full circuit passes in which everyone Passes, the round ends. You cannot Pass while Preparing.
Watching, Deceiving & Helping:
Roll one Awareness against the Stealth of anything Hiding, or against a Threshold the GM sets for a hidden object. Covers everything within 30 feet.
Critical Success As Success, but the creature moves two states. Success The creature moves one state toward Observed: Undetected becomes Hidden, Hidden becomes Concealed, Concealed becomes Observed. Failure You learn nothing. Critical Failure You commit to the wrong place. You are Wrong-Footed to that creature until your next Opportunity.

Requirements You are currently benefiting from at least Lesser Cover, or from Concealment.
Roll one Stealth against the Awareness of every creature around you (including your allies).
Critical Success You are Hidden to the creature, and they are Wrong-Footed to you until the end of the next round. Success You are Hidden to the creature. Failure They still see you. Critical Failure You have drawn the eye. You are Wrong-Footed to that creature until your next Opportunity.

Requirements You are (or believe you are) currently at least Hidden from at least one creature.
Move up to half your Speed while staying Hidden or Undetected. You must end this movement with Concealment or at least Lesser Cover from each creature you wish to remain at least Hidden from. Roll one Stealth against the Awareness of every creature to which you are currently at least Hidden (including your allies).
Critical Success You move and remain Hidden and/or Undetected, and they are Wrong-Footed to you until the end of the next round. Success You move and remain Hidden and/or Undetected. Failure You are Observed during your movement. Critical Failure You are Observed, and you are Wrong-Footed to them until your next Opportunity.
❷ Creep. As above, except: Failure You realize you would be Observed if you moved, and may choose not to move after all. Critical Failure You are Observed during your movement.

Indicate a creature you have located, whether you can see it or it is merely Hidden to you. It becomes Hidden rather than Undetected, or Concealed rather than Hidden, to any ally who can hear or see you.

Roll Intimidation against the target's Guard.
Critical Success The target is Frightened 2. Success The target is Frightened 1. Failure No effect. Critical Failure No effect, and it is emboldened: +1 Situation bonus to its Attacks against you until the end of the next round.
❷ Break Them. Critical Success The target is Frightened 3 and Heedless. Success The target is Frightened 2. Failure The target is Frightened 1. Critical Failure No effect.

Roll Guile against the target's Awareness.
Critical Success The target is Wrong-Footed to you until the end of the next round. Success The target is Wrong-Footed to you until the end of your next Opportunity. Failure No effect. Critical Failure You overcommit. You are Wrong-Footed to that creature until your next Opportunity.

Prepare ❶ at one of your Opportunities, naming one ally and the task you intend to help with. When they attempt it before your next Opportunity, use a Reaction ⓿↺ to roll a relevant check against Threshold 15.
Critical Success They gain a +2 Situation bonus. Success +1 Situation bonus. Failure No effect. Critical Failure They take a −1 Situation penalty.
Your preparation is spent whether or not they attempt the task.

Learn something true about a creature, place, or object. Possible topics include Defense Thresholds, Protection and armor materials, Weaknesses, Resistances and Immunities, Attack Thresholds, Special Abilities, and maximum Vigor.
Roll a Lore or relevant Skill check against the level-based Threshold of your target.
Critical Success You recall all facts about two topics. Success You recall all facts about one topic. Failure You recall nothing. Critical Failure You recall all (incorrect) facts about one topic.
Special You may attempt this once per target per Skill, so a character with several Lores or relevant Skills may get several angles on the same problem.
❷ Study. As above, except: Critical Failure You recall nothing.
Handling Things: Draw or stow a weapon, open a door, pull a potion from your pack, pick something up, work a lever.
Drop or let go of something you are holding.
Special: Name one creature or object Observed by you. Watch its feet, its shadow, the floor in front of it. Until your next Opportunity you gain a +2 Situation bonus to your Defenses against its effects with the Visual trait, and it is Concealed to you.

Trigger You fall past an edge, ledge, or handhold within your reach. Requirements You have a hand free; you may Release ⓿ an item as part of this Reaction to free a hand.
Roll Athletics or Acrobatics against a Threshold of 15.
Critical Success You catch it and pull yourself up in the same motion. You do not fall. Success You catch it and hang there. You are Off-Guard. Failure You fall, but the damage from the falling distance is reduced by 10 feet. Critical Failure You fall the full distance.

explorationActions: When an encounter begins, you can roll Awareness.
When an encounter begins, you can roll Athletics.
Roll an Awareness check; the GM applies it to the Thresholds to spot hidden objects and creatures. When an encounter begins, you can roll Awareness.
Every ally gains a +1 Situation bonus to initiative, and you may Step ⓿ when you roll initiative. When an encounter begins, you can roll Awareness.
Your shield begins Raised and a weapon is already in hand. When an encounter begins, you can roll Awareness.

Roll a relevant Lore or Skill check; the GM applies it to the Thresholds to potentially recall relevant information about your surroundings. When an encounter begins, you can roll the same Lore or Skill check, if the encounter is related to what you are Investigating.

Hands empty, eyes down, pace unhurried. You are not hiding. You are simply not worth watching.

Requirements You wield no weapon with a Reach greater than Adjacent, and your worn armor totals Load 1 or less.

Effects When an encounter begins, you may roll Guile for Initiative. Compare the roll against the Awareness of each enemy that you are Observed to, with the following effects:
Critical SuccessThey are Wrong-Footed to you until the end of your first Opportunity.
SuccessThey are Wrong-Footed to your first attack.
FailureNothing; they were watching you all along.
Critical FailureYou overplayed it. You are Wrong-Footed to them until your next Opportunity.

Outside an encounter, a Successful Guile check lets you approach, pass, or linger without being challenged by anyone who would otherwise have wanted to know your business.
You move quietly and keep to cover. Roll Stealth; the GM applies it to the Awareness Threshold of anyone who might notice you. When an encounter begins, you can use your Stealth roll for initiative.
downtimeActions: Move 1 already spent Talent Point to another Talent you qualify for. You cannot retrain away from a Talent in your Origin Constellation, a Root Talent, a Talent that another Talent you own requires, or a Talent that would reduce your Proficiency Rank in a Constellation.

You work with a teacher, a rival, or a manual. You gain a Flare for the particular training pursued, subject to GM approval as described in Chapter 7. You may benefit from Train only once between one Milestone and the next.

Buy and sell in a settlement. Common goods are simply available. For anything uncommon, roll a relevant Skill or Lore against a Threshold the GM sets to find someone who has one. You sell at half price.
conditions: -2 Situation to Evade and Guard against all foes.
-N to all checks and Thresholds; reduce by 1 at the end of each round.
Off-Guard, -2 to Attacks; +2 Situation to Evade vs. ranged Attacks. Stand ❶ to clear.
Off-Guard and can't Move or Step; Escape ❶ to break free.
Commitment so complete that you have stopped thinking. Maneuvers with Concentrate take 1 extra action.
As Grabbed but can’t take any action other than Escape ❶.
Lose the next N actions; may carry over across rounds.
Lose N actions at the start of each round. Reduce N by 1 at the end of each round.

−N Condition (maximum of 3) penalty to all Defense (Awareness, Endure, Evade, Guard) and Attack rolls (rolls with the Attack trait); can Travel but take no other Exploration Mode Activity. Cannot Sustain spells. Ends after ten minutes of rest, unless otherwise specified.
You’re Dying (see Chapter 4: Playing the Game). You may not necessarily be unconscious; you may merely be bleeding out or suffering a similar effect.
That Zone carries a Wound: its critical effect made lasting (see Chapter 4: Vigor and Wounds). Fill the Torso’s or Head’s Wound capacity (two, for anyone Medium or smaller) and you are Dying.

Every Hit that lands on you inflicts a Wound on the Zone it struck, and a Critical Hit inflicts two.

If you are Hit or Critically Hit and take any Nonlethal damage as a result, you are knocked unconscious. You awake in ten minutes, or sooner if someone rouses you, with 1 Vigor.
Your implement is in a neutral Bind with X’s. The Bind ends if either of you Moves, Steps, or Recenters, or when a Strike between you resolves.
X Controls your weapon. You have an Exposed Zone of X’s choice while the Bind lasts, and your attacks with that weapon take a −2 Situation penalty. Recenter ❶ or Step to end it.
You Control X’s weapon: X has an Exposed Zone of your choice. You may Close ❶ on X. The Bind ends if a third party attacks you.
You have begun a Maneuver of three or more actions: one action spent, the rest reserved. You cannot Pass; you finish or abandon at your next Opportunity. Taking a Wound abandons it.
That Zone is Exposed: Hits can land there instead of your Torso. Protection counts as 0. Recenter ❶ to clear unless otherwise stated.
Off-Guard; cannot see. Immune to Visual effects.
Cannot hear. Immune to Auditory effects.
You are out, Dying or knocked cold: you drop everything you are holding in your squares, and you’re also Prone.
zones: The target is Off-Guard until it Recenters.
If the Zone was already Exposed when a Deliberate or Committed Strike Critically Hit it, the Zone is also Wounded (see Vigor & Wounds).
The target takes a −2 Situation penalty to attack rolls until it Recenters.
If the Zone was already Exposed when a Deliberate or Committed Strike Critically Hit it, the Zone is also Wounded (see Vigor & Wounds).
The target's Speed is halved until it Recenters.
If the Zone was already Exposed when a Deliberate or Committed Strike Critically Hit it, the Zone is also Wounded (see Vigor & Wounds).
The target cannot use Reactions until it Recenters.
If the Zone was already Exposed when a Deliberate or Committed Strike Critically Hit it, the Zone is also Wounded (see Vigor & Wounds).
detection: Exactly what squares you are in, and precisely where you are positioned.
Your foe can plainly see all or most of your body.
Exactly what squares you are in, but something is preventing them from seeing or otherwise detecting all of you.
You gain a +2 Situation bonus to Evade and Guard for physical Attacks.
You are surrounded in mist, or you are in dim light, or you are hiding in foliage.
That you are present, but not what squares you occupy.
Your foe must successfully guess one of the squares you occupy in order to attack you. Even so, you gain a +4 Situation bonus to Evade and Guard for physical Attacks. Your foe is Wrong-Footed to you.
Your foe is blind, or you have succeeded on a Sneak check.
Has no idea if you are even present.
You cannot be targeted at all. Your foe is Wrong-Footed to you.
Your foe cannot see, hear, smell or feel you.
light: They are Hidden to you (or possibly Undetected, if you did not already know something was there).
cover: +1 Situation bonus to your Evade and Guard for physical Attacks.
+2 Situation bonus to your Evade and Guard for physical Attacks.
+4 Situation bonus to your Evade and Guard for physical Attacks.
You cannot be targeted at all for physical Attacks.
damageOrder: Check Immunity. Disregard damage types and effects to which the target is immune.
Add together the applicable damage dice and modifiers for each damage type.
Subtract the combined applicable Resistance from each damage type, to a minimum of 0. Apply Resistance once per damage type per damage instance, not once per die.
Add applicable Weakness to each damage type that still deals damage. Independent sources of Weakness are cumulative.

For a Zoned Attack, combine its remaining damage and subtract the struck Zone’s effective Protection once. Protection alone cannot reduce positive damage below 1. Damage already reduced to 0 remains 0.
Double the remaining damage if the Attack’s Critical Hit rules require it.
Apply the remaining damage to Vigor, or resolve it as the ability specifies. Apply associated effects at their stated timing.
protectionSteps: Armor and similar equipment provide Protection for the Zones they cover; a Zone with nothing worn there has 0.
Protection reduces damage from Zoned Attacks, once per instance, and never changes the Defense roll or the Result. Protection alone cannot reduce positive damage below 1.
Pervasive Attacks and Persistent Damage ignore ordinary Protection.
An Exposed Zone's Protection counts as 0, subject to any exception in the Attack's description; a Critical Hit against it with a Deliberate or Committed Strike inflicts a Wound.
recovery: Your Dying ends. You are conscious, on your feet if you spend an action to stand, with 1 Vigor.
Your Dying value drops by 1. If it reaches 0, your Dying ends and you are stable: still unconscious, but no longer sliding.
chargenSteps: …Your body and blood. This forms the core of your Origin Constellation and gives you starting Vigor, Speed, and unique characteristics (e.g., keen eyes).
…Vigor per level, Size, Speed, and 1 Special Ability.
…Your lineage. This adds a branch to your Origin Constellation and gives you additional unique characteristics.
…Where you were raised. This adds a branch to your Origin Constellation and gives you additional customization options.
…Starting language(s), and a bonus to Diplomacy checks with those who share your Culture.
…Your adventuring identity. This adds special techniques such as casting spells, entering a barbarian rage, sneak attacking, etc.
…Your defensive posture (Awareness, Evade, Guard, and Endure).
…Comets, which are Talent Points that can be used for any purpose (as long as you still meet the prerequisite).
damageDelivery: Beguilement; no Delivery unless it deals damage
castKinds: Immediate, generally one damage die regardless of proficiency; no extra Damage Dice. Typically one target, and no significant additional effect. Graze normally deals no damage unless the spell says otherwise.

Prepared under the normal three-action rule. Full Damage Dice according to proficiency in the spell’s parent; use the spell’s normal effects. Graze normally deals one base damage die unless the spell says otherwise.

Prepared. Normally the same full Damage Dice plus an additional capability listed by the Talent, such as a secondary effect, area, or duration. This extra capability does not automatically add a damage die.
